description:
We're taking on NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge: making the agency's

microgravity combustion archive usable for fire safety in future habitats —

lunar bases and pressurized rovers. Our plan is a dashboard that summarizes,

ranks and interprets the experiments, built on open NASA data, running offline

with no server. No prior space background needed. Wanted: Python, data

analysis, vanilla JS/SVG, visual design, and someone who can write a pitch.

PL + EN.
summary: IGNIS.py is an SI-powered fire-safety dashboard built on NASA's open microgravity combustion archive (Physical Science Informatics, PSI). The challenge says the Moon Base and pressurized rovers will likely run at 30% oxygen or more. We normalised 1,936 test points from 22 PSI tables and found that every one of the 264 solid-material tests (the fabrics, films and plastics a habitat is built from) stops at 22.7% oxygen, near 1 bar. None reaches 30%. IGNIS shows that gap on one map, lets you search every test point and open the NASA file and row behind it, and has an SI assistant that answers only from the data and says when the data cannot answer: it names the nearest real test and how far away it is. It ends with a concrete plan: publish the SoFIE-GEL ISS data in PSI, then 30 tests that would close the gap. Every number is computed from NASA's tables, and every quote is checked against its source file.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

IGNIS.py is a web dashboard over NASA's open microgravity combustion archive (Physical Science Informatics, PSI). It answers the question a lunar-habitat fire-safety engineer has to answer: is there test evidence for our cabin atmosphere? The challenge says the Moon Base and pressurized rovers will likely run at 30% oxygen or more, at 10.2 psi or less. IGNIS shows that the open archive has no solid-material test there: all 264 solid tests stop at 22.7% oxygen, near 1 bar, which is 7.3 percentage points short.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Normalisation. We mapped 22 PSI test tables from 20 accessions by hand (three pressure units, two oxygen conventions, free-text units, typo'd headers) and turned 2,870 published rows into 1,936 test points. Every rejected row is named; nothing is dropped silently.

2. Coverage map. Oxygen against pressure, with the challenge atmosphere, the solid-test ceiling, the curve of equal oxygen partial pressure and the suggested tests.

3. Ask the SI. A language model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, through a Cloudflare Worker) answers only from the corpus: it queries the test points itself and cites investigations and verbatim NASA quotes, and every source, quote and number is checked before the answer is shown. When the data cannot answer, it says so and names the nearest real test and its distance. Each answer shows how long every step took.

4. Search, Atlas and atmosphere check. Search all test points and open the NASA file and row behind any number; rank the investigations for a mission (rover, lunar base, transit cabin); check any atmosphere against the nearest evidence.

5. Test plan. Step 0: publish the SoFIE-GEL ISS data (up to 34% oxygen) in PSI. Then 30 tests: the five solid materials already burned closest to the ceiling, at three oxygen levels and two pressures. It prints as a one-page evidence-gap report. The arithmetic behind each factor (why five materials, three oxygen levels, two pressures and one test per condition) is in docs/TEST-PLAN-MATH.md, and scripts/verify_test_plan.py re-derives every figure from the test points.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

A habitat designer gets a line not to extrapolate past, the tests that would remove it, and every number traceable to a NASA row. NASA gets a cheap first step and a concrete test list. Researchers get the normalised dataset as CSV and JSON, with unit, accession and row number on every value.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Most dashboards show what data exists. IGNIS shows where it stops, and measures the distance from evidence on oxygen and pressure separately. The SI is allowed to say "the archive does not know".

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Honesty about limits: the gap is in the open archive, not in all of science. The user persona is a hypothesis; we did not interview an engineer. There is no predictive model, because above 22.7% oxygen there is no training point for solid materials. NASA certifies materials at 30% oxygen and 10.2 psia because the oxygen share drives flammability (Hirsch et al., NTRS 20090012334).

Reliability: everything except the live SI works offline from a single HTML file; if the SI does not answer within 25 seconds, a saved real answer is shown with its date.

TOOLS

Python 3 (standard library only), vanilla JavaScript, HTML, CSS and SVG; Cloudflare Workers; OpenRouter (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash); GitHub Pages. Code under the MIT licence, data CC0-1.0. One command, sh scripts/check_all.sh, rebuilds the data and re-checks every number, every quote and the test-plan arithmetic.
